key_insight: Free-electron-driven van der Waals crystals generate linearly polarized X-rays with polarization controlled by crystal orientation, offering a route to compact X-ray spectroscopy.
engineering_relevance: Compact polarized X-ray sources could broaden access to material characterization for photovoltaics, catalysis and optoelectronics; this is not an AI solar-cell study.
method: Theoretically model and experimentally demonstrate polarized X-ray generation from electron-driven van der Waals crystals.
Reorient the crystal to control polarization without additional polarizers.
Propose orientation-controlled XANES (ORIXANES) using polarized X-rays with larger spectral linewidths.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experimental generation, high polarization across perpendicular-to-in-plane angles, and intensities exceeding 10^9 photons s⁻¹ sr⁻¹ mA⁻¹; synchrotron-comparable XANES is presented as a proposed scheme.
watch_item: Practical ORIXANES performance with broader spectral linewidths requires validation beyond the proposed scheme.
paper_title: Polarized X-rays from table-top free-electron-driven van der Waals crystals
